Subject: Renewal discussion and proposed capacity uplift

Hi Dylan,

We're starting to plan KiteLabs' contract renewal for Q1. Usage has grown faster than anticipated — we expect a 40-55% uplift in inference volume next 12 months driven by new feature launches. We'd like to discuss:

- Pricing for an adjusted commit that covers the uplift (mix of retainer + burst).
- A short-term price-hold for 6 months while we onboard a new model pipeline.
- A step-down credit schedule if actual usage falls below thresholds in the first quarter.

Can we get a first-pass proposal this week? Procurement wants to see a term sheet and indicative credit/discount figures before scheduling a renewal call.

Thanks,
Sam Park
Head of Platform
KiteLabs

Hi Sam — thanks for the note and congrats on the product momentum. I talked with our pricing team and sketched a flexible structure to cover the uplift while protecting KiteLabs on spend. High-level proposal below (attachment: term sheet v1).

Proposal (first pass):
- 12-month term with a blended commit model: 60% monthly retainer (reserved throughput) + 40% burst pool.
- 6-month price-hold for the committed unit rate for the first 6 months post-sign; after that we move to tiered pricing tied to monthly consumption bands.
- Step-down credits: if average monthly usage for months 1–3 is <85% of commit, KiteLabs receives a prorated credit up to 15% of monthly invoice for that period (applied as one-time credit).
- Upsell trigger: if usage exceeds commit by >60% for two consecutive months, we auto-provision + notify and cap burst overage at negotiated rate for the following month while we formalize commit increase.

I want to bring in a quick internal approvals/ops thread to confirm how the credits interact with billing and whether we can attach an SLA-exception for burst provisioning. Looping in Monica (Sales Ops) and Laura (VP Sales) to confirm operational feasibility.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Wednesday 12/02 to walk through the term sheet and adjust numbers? I'll share a cleaned term sheet and a usage workbook.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Dylan / Monica — quick responses inline: 

- Price-hold: okay to do 6 months on the committed unit rate, provided we include a mid-term usage review at month 3 with both sides and a one-time reprice clause if model mix materially changes (>20% change in GPU-seconds per request).

- Auto-provision + capped overage: Operations can support auto-provision for 1 month with capped overage rate, but we need the customer to agree to a follow-up action: formal update to commit or a notified downgrade. Ops will require a written SLA-exception for priority provisioning and a documented MA (mutual action) in the term sheet. Monica — can you add the language.

- Step-down credit as invoice credit: finance prefers invoice credits. Max 15% is acceptable, but credits should be reconciled in month 4 and issued as a single credit line on the next invoice. We should disallow stacking with any ad-hoc promotional credits.

- Discount ceiling: up to 22% on committed units for this ARR band if they sign a 12-month commit and agree to the usage review clause. Any additional concessions must be escalated to me.

Approve moving this to a clean v3 term-sheet for the customer. Dylan — please incorporate the SLAs, credit reconciliation timing, and discount ceiling into v3 and loop in Finance if they push back.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — thanks for the patience. Attached is a cleaned term sheet (v3) and an anonymized usage workbook showing the proposed commit bands and expected spend. Summary of key changes per our internal review: 

- 12-month term; blended commit (60% retainer / 40% burst) as discussed.
- 6-month price-hold on committed unit rates; 3-month review checkpoint; one-time reprice clause if model mix changes >20%.
- Step-down credit: invoice credit reconciled in month 4, up to 15% of relevant invoices for months 1–3, non-stackable.
- Auto-provisioning: Ops will auto-provision burst capacity for up to 1 month with capped overage rate; this requires a signed SLA-exception (included in v3).
- Discount ceiling on committed units: 22% (requires 12-month commit).

Next steps:
1) Review the attached KiteLabs_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf and usage_breakdown_Q1-Q3.xlsx and confirm comments by 12/17 so procurement can route for legal.
2) If terms look good, we'll prepare a DocuSign agreement and schedule the 30-min handoff call to finalize operational onboarding.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a call if you'd like line-by-line walk-through.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
